findings.title: Several parent-owned RED cases are still absent or test a different condition
findings.evidence: In tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:1654-1678, the alleged case-1 delayed dependency is explicitly asserted to be one applicationBatch source, so it never creates distinct author-sequence n and n+1 vertices or demonstrates n+1 being withheld because n is missing. creatorFenceScan at lines 1556-1613 covers a large valid fence and m > f, but never supplies the required m <= prior terminalThrough fence. No settlement-profile test leaves a newly admitted null-boundary member with neither a fence nor slot 0 and closes successfully; the case-17 mapping points only to the ordinary v1 control. The genesis checks assert admissionEpoch=0 but do not pin the required creator slot-0 accounting. Closed codec cases 18 and 26-27 do not own these missing runtime cases.
findings.impact: A GREEN implementation could use an observed maximum instead of a contiguous dependency prefix, mishandle stale fences, or incorrectly reject/advance a null boundary while the current parent test still passes. The committed test therefore does not yet close the complete parent case matrix required by the accepted design.
findings.required_action: Before production GREEN, add a tests-only correction using two genuinely distinct causally linked author sequences for case 1, an m <= terminalThrough fence for case 12, the settlement null/no-fence/no-slot-0 close plus the retained v1 refusal for case 17, and an exact creator slot-0 frontier assertion for case 22. Keep the existing causal terminus and do not fabricate checkpoint or ingress authority.

findings.title: Manual-review resolution is neither tested nor currently defined by an existing product seam
findings.evidence: Accepted design RED case 11 requires that resolving a manual-review hold later completes the plan. manualReviewHold at test lines 1505-1553 proves only the hold, another author's progress, and retained source custody, then closes both sessions. In examples/v3-room/src/index.ts, settlementHold is released only by shutdown (creation at 2004-2007; release at 4319), while writeMergedSettlementPlan rejects a changed prior disposition as 'v3 room settlement plan source differs' around 2932-2944. The public session exposes no demonstrated resolver in this RED.
findings.impact: GREEN cannot honestly satisfy the accepted case-11 lifecycle from the current test and source contract. Implementing a resolver or allowing a manual-review disposition transition without first freezing its authority and idempotence semantics could silently introduce new product behavior or a public API.
findings.required_action: Freeze and test a genuine resolution path using an already-authorized existing input/internal authority if one exists. If completion requires a new API, authority carrier, or new disposition-transition contract, stop and reslice that decision under the user's API-review rule rather than adding it inside f5b GREEN.

findings.title: Case 25 does not prove absence of duplicate publication
findings.evidence: ambiguousPlanIssue at lines 936-1009 checks row/link atomicity, lineage, owner deactivation, retry counts, one durable plan effect, one disposition, and one creator application effect. Its publication assertion at lines 973-976 checks only that subsequent publications use a different handle; it never counts publications for the recovered candidate sequence and digest. Both committed and uncommitted fence/replacement matrices could therefore publish the final row more than once without failing this helper.
findings.impact: The prompt's required no-duplicate issue/link/disposition/publication/application guarantee is incomplete precisely at the ambiguous transaction window, allowing an accidental duplicate network publication to escape the parent GREEN gate.
findings.required_action: For every committed/neither fence and replacement outcome, assert the exact publication count and identity for the surviving sequence/digest, alongside the existing exact row/link, retry, disposition, and application-effect checks. Preserve the separately accepted replayable external-notification contract rather than conflating it with outbox publication.

findings.title: The 64-writer golden-path continuation does not account for every required plan and fence
findings.evidence: sixtyFourWriterGoldenPath does establish 64 ACL members, 256 baseline applications across epochs 0-3, six selected displaced sources, rotating offline cohorts, three transitions, restart/reopen, publication evidence, checkpoint lineage, and selected source-to-replacement links. However, plan/fence assertions at lines 1138-1152 run only for the six selected displaced owners. The other retained writers can reopen and issue their baseline operation without any assertion that a durable empty plan preceded issue or that exactly one current-epoch fence was issued and published, despite the accepted design requiring a fence at every open/adopt after drain. Final cold-reopen state at lines 1280-1283 is compared only after sorting by clientOperationId rather than against exact canonical product-state bytes.
findings.impact: A regression that skips or duplicates empty-plan fences for most writers, issues before durable plan creation, or changes final application ordering could pass the advertised 64-writer proof. That is insufficient for the explicit plan-link and exact-state golden-path requirement.
findings.required_action: Add per-author/per-epoch accounting for the durable plan revision, fenceSequence, exact one fence commit/publication before the first ordinary issue, and the six selected replacement links. Also compare exact canonical application-state bytes after the final cold reopen, retaining the semantic digest as an additional check rather than a replacement.

findings.title: The per-peer activation isolation is a hybrid realm rather than a complete physical-client realm
findings.evidence: The mock at test lines 99-139 query-isolates only creator-adoption-activate.ts. Its imported creator-adoption, v3-live, creator-adoption-intent, and creator-successor-live modules remain shared through the unqueried module graph, so capability-producing WeakMaps and other module owners are not isolated as they would be in separate browser globals. The test does preserve unchanged activation source, distinct activeOwners maps, real bindings, same-peer restart reuse, and no singleton reset or fabricated result.
findings.impact: This is adequate to remove the demonstrated activeOwners false collision, but it should not be represented as full independent-process/browser-realm proof and could miss another client-local singleton coupling outside creator-adoption-activate.
findings.required_action: Owner: the final retained/isolated browser gate. Preserve this bounded fixture for RED, but require one genuine multi-context or isolated-client retained proof before closing the 64-writer golden-path claim, or explicitly limit the claim to activation-owner isolation.

findings.title: The unexecuted continuation has an unproven 60-second aggregate timeout
findings.evidence: The first settlement test puts the 64-client/four-epoch workload, hundreds of database transfers/reopens, all fault helpers, pruning, re-entry, and ambiguity matrices into one test with a 60,000 ms timeout at line 1750. RED stops after roughly 418 ms at the first close, so no evidence establishes that the complete continuation can run within that bound.
findings.impact: After the causal product seam is fixed, a fixture-cost timeout could obscure the next semantic result and turn the GREEN loop into timing diagnosis rather than deterministic TDD.
findings.required_action: Owner: parent test infrastructure. Before final GREEN closure, split independently attributable continuations into bounded tests while preserving the exact workload, or record one complete focused duration and use a documented non-product timeout that is not treated as a product performance threshold.

causal_red_assessment: The accepted RED is genuinely causal. The real room performs ordinary issue, durable issuance, publication, creator ingress, and genuine creator close preparation. The wrapper is reached only after the real close reports exact 'creator close actor failed: CERTIFIED_VALUE_MISMATCH'; it then pins the five actual hard-coded profile sites. No future export, checkpoint bytes, settlement capability, activation success, or forged record is supplied. The complete v1 issue/close/adopt/cold-reopen/issue and stale-floor control passes. RED causality is therefore accepted even though downstream settlement continuations remain unexecuted.
coverage_assessment: The correction materially improves coverage: delayed/unpublished fence and replacement paths, partial-progress preservation, same-key re-entry, stale-head refusal, displaced controls, positive prune ownership, ambiguity, three transitions, and the 64-writer workload are executable continuations, while exact codec cases 18 and 26-27 remain correctly assigned to closed prerequisites. It is not yet coverage-complete because cases 1, 11, 12, 17, 22 and case-25 publication accounting have the blocking gaps described above.
realm_assessment: The query-isolated activation module faithfully exercises unchanged production activation behavior and preserves one activeOwners singleton per modeled client, same-peer reuse, real bindings, and opaque capability checks. It neither resets the singleton nor returns a fake activation. It is nevertheless a hybrid shared-dependency graph, so it is acceptable for this causal RED but not by itself a complete physical-client/browser-realm golden-path proof.
golden_path_assessment: The test now models one genuine 64-member room, all 64 writers contributing in each of epochs 0-3, three rotating eight-writer offline cohorts, six pending/published displaced sources, three close/adopt transitions, selected creator restart, repeated peer cold reopen, checkpoint lineage, ACL/authority checks, and aggregate application accounting. Membership alone is not substituted for contribution. The missing universal plan/fence accounting and exact final canonical state comparison still prevent this RED from fully freezing the MMORPG-scale functional acceptance.
scope_api_assessment: The demonstrated profile failure and most intended GREEN work fit existing private seams: make all five protocol successor/checkpoint sites profile-aware through settlementProfileFor, compose the settlement checkpoint instead of legacy controls, thread the authenticated frontier into readSettlementSources/openProgressSources, permit the already-existing signer-plus-declaration input combination only for settlement and rebind close authority, and invoke existing authenticated pruning maintenance from its product owner. None inherently requires a new wire field, crypto, dependency, threshold, or public API. Manual-review resolution is the unresolved exception: current source has no demonstrated completion seam, so it must be specified through existing authority or explicitly resliced before implementation.

All requested manifests validate and exclude themselves; the design manifest correctly has three entries. Commits 0c59869a, 3a9e9329, 1dcff170, 8fcbc039 and cecde972 are signed and test-only. The histories are represented honestly: 1dcff170 and 8fcbc039 are rejected 2-failed/0-passed fixture runs; cecde972 is the accepted 1-failed/1-passed causal matrix; the earlier 0c59869a rejection is also preserved. The three external live-snapshot diagnostics are explicitly disclosed rather than misrepresented as a full repository typecheck pass.
